dataset_info.name: VEDA AyurMind AI — Diseases & Therapeutic Herbs Dataset (Source: Dravyaguna Vijnana Vol. 2)
dataset_info.part_description: DIS-146 to DIS-210 — Diseases from PDF-2 (Abortifacient to Cyst/Tumour)
dataset_info.source_text: Dravyaguna Vijnana — Therapeutic Indication of Drugs (Second Volume, Pages 729-754)
dataset_info.description: Part 4 of the VEDA disease database. Extracted from the second Dravyaguna Vijnana volume. This volume introduces many new herbs not in Volume 1 including Kulattha, Langali, Nimba, Marica, Madhuka, Kantakari, Karavellaka, Kiratatikta and others. Disease IDs continue from DIS-145 (last entry in Parts 1-3).

diseases.description: Substances that induce termination of pregnancy. This volume adds Langali to the previous list, a potent alkaloid-rich herb used in classical Ayurvedic toxicology and gynaecology.
Localised collection of pus in body tissue. This volume adds Karanja and Kumari (Aloe vera) to the formulation, both well-known for anti-infective and wound-healing properties.
Diminished digestive fire (Agni) causing sluggish digestion and Ama accumulation. This volume adds Karanja (Kantaki), Kupilu (Nux vomica) and Marica (black pepper) — powerful digestive stimulants.

associated_sanskrit_terms.meaning: Food intoxication associated with faulty digestion and impaired metabolism

diseases.description: Chronic excessive alcohol consumption causing physical and mental derangement. Same formulation as Volume 1.

associated_sanskrit_terms.meaning: Alcoholism; effect of excessive use of alcohol

diseases.description: Loss of hair from scalp or body. This volume adds Kakadani and Langali to the formulation. Langali (Gloriosa superba) has strong local stimulating action on hair follicles.

associated_sanskrit_terms.meaning: Promoting skin health; palliative for skin diseases

diseases.description: Painful joint condition from Ama accumulation with Vata vitiation; correlates with rheumatoid arthritis. This volume adds Kulattha (horse gram), Lakuca, Mulaka and Mundi — additional anti-Ama and anti-inflammatory herbs.

associated_sanskrit_terms.meaning: Food intoxication associated with faulty digestion and impaired metabolism
Group of diseases caused by aggravated Vata — pain, convulsion, paralysis

diseases.description: Hyperacidity with burning sensation, abdominal pain and biliary nausea. This volume adds Katuki, Narikela (coconut) and Nimba (neem) — bitter hepatoprotective and cooling herbs.

associated_sanskrit_terms.meaning: Acid gastritis; hyperacidity with burning sensation, abdominal pain, biliary nausea

diseases.description: Deficiency of red blood cells or haemoglobin causing pallor and fatigue. This volume adds Draksa, Kakadani, Pancamula (laghu), Madhuka, Matulunga and Mulaka — rich nutrient and blood-building herbs.

associated_sanskrit_terms.meaning: Anti-anaemic; indicated in treatment of anaemia
Nourishing and promoting body tissues; nutrient tissue homologues

diseases.description: Loss of appetite and lack of desire to eat. Same formulation as Volume 1.
Tuberculous infection of cervical lymph nodes. This volume adds Langali, Madhuka and Mundi to the classical herbs Bhallataka and Bhrngaraja.

associated_sanskrit_terms.meaning: Cervical adenitis; chain of swollen glands in neck
Glandular enlargement, swelling and other symptoms

diseases.description: Substances promoting sexual vigour, potency and libido. This volume greatly expands the list with Kapikacchu, Karkatasrngi, Kokilaksa, Masa, Masaparni, Mudgaparni, Munjataka and Musali — all classical Vajikara herbs from the Jivaniya and Shukrala groups.
Inflammation of joints with pain and stiffness. This volume adds Ketaki (Pandanus odoratissimus) to Indravaruni and Guggulu.

associated_sanskrit_terms.meaning: Disease caused by vitiation of Vata and Rakta; gout
Group of diseases caused by aggravated Vata — pain, convulsion, paralysis

diseases.description: Chronic bronchial asthma with breathlessness and wheezing. This volume adds Mamsi, Marica, Matulunga, Mulaka, Nirgundi, Kadali, Kakodumbara, Kantakari, Karkatasrngi, Karpura, Kasamarda, Kusmanda and Kulattha — making this the most comprehensive Svasa formulation in both volumes.
Pathological state of excessive digestive fire causing rapid burning of body tissues, severe hunger and emaciation. Single herb — Apamarga.

associated_sanskrit_terms.meaning: Excessive hunger and digestion causing loss of dhatus, emaciation and debility

diseases.description: Tissue injury from heat or fire. This volume adds Narikela (coconut), Madhuka and Dhataki alongside Asvattha and Kumari (Aloe vera) — the latter being the premier burn-healing plant in Ayurveda.
Generalised or localised burning sensation; Pitta aggravation. This volume adds Karkandhu-Badara, Mallika and Nimba to the formulation.

Hard mineral deposits in kidneys or urinary tract. This volume significantly expands the list with Kalamba, Kantakari, Karkota, Kataka, Katukalabu, Ksirivrksa, Kulattha, Kunduru, Kusa, Kusumbha, Mamsi, Matulunga, Mayurasikhа, Morata and Kola-Badara.

associated_sanskrit_terms.meaning: Calculus; stone — Mutra-ashmari (urinary) and Pitta-ashmari (gall bladder)

diseases.description: Small sand-like micro-calculi causing irritation during urination. This volume adds Kadamba, Karavira and Narikela.
Pain or discomfort in the chest region. Same formulation as Volume 1.

associated_sanskrit_terms.meaning: Chest pain; colic pain in iliac or pelvic region

diseases.description: Severe spasmodic abdominal pain from intestinal gas or Vata accumulation. This volume adds Kantakikaranja, Kulattha, Laghu-pancamula and Lavanga (clove) to the formulation.

associated_sanskrit_terms.meaning: Colic; ache; pain; disease or symptom

diseases.description: Pulmonary tuberculosis with chronic cough, weight loss and haemoptysis. This volume adds Kakajangha, Kharjura, Kusmanda, Laghupancamula, Madayanti, Madhuka, Mandukaparni, Mulaka, Nagabala and Nirgundi — rasayana and lung-nourishing herbs.

associated_sanskrit_terms.meaning: Wasting condition of body due to chest-wound

diseases.description: Acute nasal inflammation with running nose and sneezing. This volume adds Kantakari, Madhulika, Mandukaparni, Marica and Mulaka.

associated_sanskrit_terms.meaning: Curing and improving throat disorders; soothing to throat

diseases.description: Herbs used for skin care, complexion improvement and beauty enhancement. This volume adds Madayanti (henna), Mallika, Ketaki, Narikela and Nimbuka (lemon) — all fragrant and complexion-improving herbs.

associated_sanskrit_terms.meaning: Useful in promoting complexion of the skin (pigmentation)
Promoting skin health; palliative for skin diseases

diseases.description: Acute or chronic cough; dry or productive. This is the most comprehensive formulation across both volumes — 50+ herbs including Kakadani, Kakamaci, Kakodumbara, Kamala, Kantakari, Karkatasrngi, Karpasa, Kasamarda, Khadira, Kharjura, Kulattha, Kusmanda, Kutaja, Madhulika, Brhat pancamula, Mandukaparni, Marica, Masaparni, Mudga, Mudgaparni, Mulaka, Mustaka and Nirgundi.
Abnormal tissue growth; cystic or tumorous mass. This volume adds Madhuka and Mulaka to the formulation.

associated_sanskrit_terms.meaning: Abdominal lump caused by accumulation of wind and other causes

diseases.description: Substances used to remove unwanted body hair. This volume adds Kosataki, Kusumbha, Madhuka and Mulaka to Bhallataka.

associated_sanskrit_terms.meaning: Promoting skin health; palliative for skin diseases

diseases.description: Frequent loose or watery stools. This volume adds Kancata, Kapittha, Karpasa, Kasmarya, Katphala, Kesaraja, Kutaja, Laghu-Pancamula, Laja, Lonika, Mallika, Masura, Mocarasa, Mulaka, Mustaka and Nicula to the extensive formulation.

associated_sanskrit_terms.meaning: Disorders of intestinal tract; malabsorption syndrome

diseases.description: Various oral cavity disorders including stomatitis and ulcers. This volume adds Khadira, Lavanga and Mamsi — classical oral antiseptics and anti-infectives.

associated_sanskrit_terms.meaning: Indicated or useful to cleanse the mouth
Inflamed gums with haemorrhage and foul smell

diseases.description: Inflammation of oral mucous membrane; mouth ulcers (aphthous ulcers).
Inflammation of the tonsils (palatine tonsils); sore throat, pain on swallowing and fever. New entry in Volume 2.

associated_sanskrit_terms.meaning: Curing and improving throat disorders; soothing to throat

diseases.description: Stiffness or palsy of the tongue impairing speech and swallowing. New specific entry in Volume 2.

Anti-vata; indicated in diseases of nervous system

diseases.description: Soft tissue growths (polyps) in the nasal cavity causing obstruction and chronic nasal symptoms. New specific entry in Volume 2.
Various tooth and gum disorders. This volume adds Ksirivrksa and Nimba alongside classical dental herbs.

associated_sanskrit_terms.meaning: Dentrifice; promoting teeth or dental health; curing dental ailments

diseases.description: Tooth decay from bacterial acid erosion. This volume adds Kakajangha, Kamala, Katutumbi and Matulunga to the dental caries formulation.
Teeth loosening from periodontal disease or nutritional deficiency. Adds Mustaka.
Symptoms during teething in infants — pain, fever, irritability. New specific entry in Volume 2.
Tooth pain from decay, infection or nerve exposure. Adds Haritamanjari (fresh Haritaki flower buds) — a new herb for dental pain.

associated_sanskrit_terms.meaning: Colic; ache; pain; disease or symptom

diseases.description: Altered or abnormal taste sensation in the mouth; may indicate systemic disease, nutritional deficiency or medication side effect. New specific entry in Volume 2.

associated_sanskrit_terms.meaning: Tastelessness of mouth; tasteless state of vocal cavity (mouth orific-tongue taste sense)

diseases.description: Various throat disorders including pharyngitis, laryngitis and diphtheria. Same formulation as Volume 1.

associated_sanskrit_terms.meaning: Diphtheria; infectious disease of throat and air passage
Curing, cleaning and improving throat disorders; soothing to throat

diseases.description: General gynaecological conditions. This volume lists Dasamula, Mundi and Pippali as general stri roga herbs.
Absence of menstruation. This volume adds Kulattha and Kumari (Aloe vera) to the formulation.

associated_sanskrit_terms.meaning: Excessive discharge of menstrual blood; menorrhagia

diseases.description: Abnormal white or yellowish vaginal discharge. This volume adds Lodhra and Asoka to the formulation — classical stambhaka (astringent) herbs for female reproductive tract.
Inflammation of breast tissue often during lactation. This volume adds Kumari (Aloe vera) — known for soothing and anti-inflammatory local application.

Abnormally heavy or prolonged menstrual bleeding. This volume significantly expands the formulation adding Kadali, Kakodumbara, Keteki, Kusa, Laksa, Madhuka and Nagakesara — additional haemostatic and uterine tonic herbs.

associated_sanskrit_terms.meaning: Excessive discharge of menstrual blood; menorrhagia

diseases.description: Post-partum complications after childbirth. This volume adds Nirgundi alongside Dasamula.
A woman's disease causing increased urinary flow with incontinence, dehydration and debility; variously interpreted as gynaecological, hormonal or metabolic disease. Adds Kadali and Kumuda.

associated_sanskrit_terms.meaning: A woman's disease causing increased flow of urine with incontinence and consequent dehydration and debility

diseases.description: Inability to conceive. This volume adds Kantakari Sveta (white variety), Masaparni and Nagakesara — specific Shukrala (semen-promoting) herbs.

Condition of lax or hypotonic vaginal musculature.

Excessive sleepiness or reduced alertness during waking hours. Kapha and Tamas predominance.
Intestinal inflammation with bloody mucus diarrhoea, cramps and tenesmus. This volume adds Kantaki-karanja, Lakuca, Lodhra, Lonika and Marica.

Discharge of pus or fluid from the ear indicating active infection. This volume adds Karpasa.

associated_sanskrit_terms.meaning: Promoting body strength; muscular strength; resistance to diseases; tonic

diseases.description: Substances inducing therapeutic emesis (Vamana karma) in Panchakarma for Kapha elimination. This volume adds Aristaka, Madana and Madhulaka to Jimuta.

associated_sanskrit_terms.meaning: Emetic; aid to emetics or emesis
Purification; radical elimination of morbid substances

diseases.description: Recurrent seizures from abnormal brain electrical activity. This volume adds Ketaki, Kumari, Madana, Mamsi, Kantakari, Karavira, Kasa and Kataka to the formulation.

diseases.description: Multiple erupting vesicular skin boils. This volume adds Kirata (Swertia chirata), Karanja and Khadira — bitter and anti-infective herbs.
